planIdentity.covers: sha256 of the plan serialized by the compiler's canonical writer (ASCII JSON, two-space indent, trailing newline) with planIdentity removed

freshnessPolicies.rule: Evidence comes from a live provider or deployed-site run of the exact candidate source commit, in the run named by the ledger (run_id and source_sha match).
freshnessPolicies.reuseCondition: never reused: a new commit, a new run or a new deployment requires a new live run

freshnessPolicies.rule: Independent review evidence names the reviewed commit; it is fresh only for that commit, or for a later commit whose diff since the reviewed commit touches none of the reviewed paths, as stated by the reviewer.
freshnessPolicies.reuseCondition: not reused by the verifier; a re-review (or a reviewer's no-change attestation) is new evidence

freshnessPolicies.rule: Process and owner evidence is a record written to the run's own Praxis event log during the run (or a CI-observed owner attestation from the run), bound to the exact candidate commit; records about another candidate or another run do not count.
freshnessPolicies.reuseCondition: never reused: each candidate needs its own records; verify-process rejects evidence bound to another candidate

freshnessPolicies.rule: Evidence comes from a deterministic test (unit, property, fixture replay, offline browser) whose result depends only on its declared inputs.
freshnessPolicies.reuseCondition: reusable within one run only when the test identity and the digest of every declared input (tested source paths, fixtures, dependency lock, baseline sha256) are unchanged and Dokimos reports the evidence Reusable:true with matching id, digest and immutable revision; never reused from an earlier rehearsal

evidenceContract.digest: sha256 of the evidence file bytes equals its entry in the independently pinned evidence manifest
evidenceContract.reuse: Reuse is permitted only when Dokimos reports the evidence Reusable:true with matching id, SHA-256 digest and immutable revision, and no invalidatedBy condition has occurred since; otherwise the check is re-run. Evidence from earlier rehearsals is never reused for this run.
evidenceContract.obligationEvidence: An obligation counts as verified only from an evidence file that passes every check above for its requirement and lists, under `obligations`, an entry {id: <the obligation's VPO id>, verification: PASS, tests: [{testId, outcome: passed}]} whose tests are bound to that obligation in this plan; the categories of those tests must cover every required category. A passing requirement-level result, or a test bound to a different obligation, verifies nothing.

exclusionPolicy.rule: A P0 requirement leaves scope only through an exclusion listed in curation/verification-plan.json whose approval is an authenticated operator change {requirement_id, action: exclude} in the pinned approvals file. It stays in the plan, marked excluded with its approval; any other exclusion fails compilation (V18).

categories.definition: Deterministic tests of one component in isolation (F# unit and property tests, illegal-transition and forged-history variants); no browser, provider or network.
categories.producer: test run of the application (Dokimos / CI test job)

categories.definition: Tests across a boundary between components or systems: producer/consumer contract tests, recorded-response provider contract tests, storage golden replay, dependency compatibility smoke, catalog verification.
categories.producer: test run of the application (Dokimos / CI test job)

categories.definition: The application exercised in a real browser engine (WebKit/Chromium via Percepta or Playwright), offline-fixture or deployed, including printed and rendered output.
categories.producer: browser test run (Percepta / Playwright in CI)

categories.definition: Real requests against the authorized live provider (the GitHub test repository) in the candidate's own run, with independent re-reads; mocked or recorded responses never count.
categories.producer: live provider test run in the candidate's own CI run

categories.definition: Evidence that a security property holds: credential handling, least privilege, secret non-disclosure in logs, URLs, screenshots and artifacts.
categories.producer: security test run or security review record

categories.definition: Accessibility verification: automated accessibility report (axe), keyboard-only and focus checks, reduced motion, screen-reader semantics.
categories.producer: accessibility test run or accessibility review record

categories.definition: Evidence produced by a party independent of the implementing agent: an independent reviewer's record, or an acceptance job the implementer does not author, bound to the reviewed or deployed SHA.
categories.producer: independent reviewer record (Praxis work evidence --kind independent-review) or an acceptance job the implementer does not author

categories.definition: A record of how the work was carried out, written while it happened to the run's Praxis event log: assignment, execution start, checkpoints, dependency decisions, scope changes, release-candidate selection, test-result and acceptance references. A record the tooling observed (a verified checkpoint, CI automation) or a statement an agent made, bound to the candidate; never a reviewer finding or an owner decision.
categories.producer: Praxis work event log of the rehearsal repository (work start, work checkpoint, work evidence)

categories.definition: A decision that only the owner or an authorized human may make, recorded by that human and backed by an attestation the verifier checks against the frozen rules (for example a pull-request review by the owner's login, fetched by CI). A decision an agent transcribed is an agent assertion and never counts.
categories.producer: owner-approval records in the Praxis work event log, with CI-observed attestations

evidenceCategories.rule: An obligation requires the union of the categories of every rule whose conditions all hold for it. No rule: unclassified (missing coverage), never a default.

scopeDecisions.amendmentRule: An obligation's acceptance criterion is amended only by an authenticated operator change {obligation_id, action: amend, criterion, rationale} in the pinned approvals file, listed in curation obligationAmendments with the owner decision it applies. The baseline text stays verbatim beside the amendment. An amendment changes what the bound tests must prove; it never verifies the obligation and never removes it from scope. Any other amendment fails compilation (V18) and makes verify-plan INVALID (UNAUTHORIZED-AMENDMENT).
scopeDecisions.derivationRule: A derived obligation restates other obligations. Each clause is verbatim in its text, and the clauses account for all of it except the declared connectives. A clause names the in-scope P0 obligations that must be verified for it; a residual clause (one that names none, or is marked direct because its constituents prove less than it states) is also proven by the derived obligation's own bound tests. Connectives come from a fixed vocabulary. Which obligation states a clause is a review judgement (AR-034-O2), not something the compiler can decide. The derived obligation is verified only when its own required categories are covered and every constituent obligation is verified (constituent-unverified otherwise).
